ZCOUNT.explanation: ZCOUNT checks one sorted set and counts members whose scores fall between the two given bounds. Both ends include their values by default, but you can exclude an end with a leading parenthesis.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key that contains the sorted set.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: The lowest score. It is inclusive unless it starts with `(`; use `-inf` for no lower limit.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The highest score. It is inclusive unless it starts with `(`; use `+inf` for no upper limit.

ZCOUNT.returns: An integer: the number of members in the selected score range.

example.title: Count a score range
example.code:
ZADD scores 10 "Ada"
ZADD scores 20 "Lin"
ZADD scores 30 "Mina"
ZCOUNT scores 10 20
example.explanation: This returns 2 because the members with scores 10 and 20 are both counted.

useCases.title: Range checks
useCases.scenario: Count members with scores in a permitted numeric interval.

useCases.title: Full-set counts
useCases.scenario: Count all members by using `-inf` and `+inf`.

useCases.title: Threshold queries
useCases.scenario: Count only scores above or below a threshold with an exclusive bound.

interview.question: What does ZCOUNT do?
interview.answer: ZCOUNT returns the number of members in a sorted set whose scores are in the requested range. Its syntax is `ZCOUNT key min max`.
interview.followUp: How does it scale? It runs in O(log(N)), where N is the number of sorted-set elements, rather than scanning every member.

interview.question: How do you make a score bound exclusive?
interview.answer: The default range is inclusive at both ends. Prefix a limit with `(` to exclude that endpoint, such as `(10`.
interview.followUp: How would you count every member with a score greater than 10? Use `ZCOUNT key (10 +inf`.

interview.question: What does ZCOUNT return?
interview.answer: The command returns an integer containing the number of members in the selected score range. It is a read-only command in the `@read` and `@sortedset` ACL categories.
interview.followUp: What happens if the range covers all possible scores? Use `-inf` and `+inf`; the result is the sorted set's member count.

keyPoints: It counts sorted-set members whose scores are between `min` and `max`.
Its score-bound rules match those used by `ZRANGEBYSCORE`.
The operation is O(log(N)) because Redis uses element ranks to locate the range.
Redis Open Source has supported this command since version 2.0.0.
gotchas: The limits include their boundary scores unless you prefix that limit with `(`.
Use `-inf` as the lower limit or `+inf` as the upper limit when the range should have no bound.

ZINCRBY.summary: ZINCRBY adds a number to a member's score in a Redis sorted set. It creates a missing member and returns the resulting score.
ZINCRBY.explanation: ZINCRBY adds the given numeric increment to a member's current score in a sorted set. If the member is missing, Redis creates it with the increment as its initial score. A negative increment lowers the score, and the command returns the resulting score.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The name of the key containing the sorted set.

parameters.name: increment
parameters.description: The numeric amount to add to the current score.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: The sorted-set member whose score changes.

ZINCRBY.returns: The member's new score. RESP2 returns it as a bulk string containing a double-precision floating-point number; RESP3 returns a double.

example.title: Increase a sorted-set score
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 10 "alice"
ZINCRBY leaderboard 2 "alice"
ZRANGE leaderboard 0 -1 WITHSCORES
example.explanation: This creates Alice with score 10, adds 2 to her score, then reads the members and scores.

useCases.title: Leaderboards
useCases.scenario: Add points to a player's existing leaderboard score.

useCases.title: Ranked counters
useCases.scenario: Increase or decrease a counter while keeping items ordered by score.

useCases.title: Priority updates
useCases.scenario: Adjust a priority value as work moves through a queue.

interview.question: What does ZINCRBY do, and what is its complexity?
interview.answer: ZINCRBY changes one member's score in a sorted set and returns the new score. Its time complexity is O(log(N)), where N is the number of sorted-set elements.
interview.followUp: What happens if the member is absent? Redis adds it, using the increment as its starting score.

interview.question: What are the arguments to ZINCRBY?
interview.answer: The command has three arguments: the sorted-set key, the numeric increment, and the member. The member's current score increases by that amount.
interview.followUp: Can the score decrease? Yes. Pass a negative increment.

interview.question: What does ZINCRBY return?
interview.answer: RESP2 returns the new score as a bulk string containing a double-precision floating-point number. RESP3 returns the new score as a double.
interview.followUp: What does the command return when a new member is created? It returns the increment, which is the member's initial score.

keyPoints: It updates the score of one sorted-set member.
The key argument identifies the sorted set to change.
The increment is added to the member's existing score.
The member argument selects which sorted-set entry to update.
A missing member is created with the increment as its first score.
The operation takes logarithmic time relative to the sorted-set size.
The result is the member's updated score.
gotchas: Use a negative increment when you want to lower a member's score.
The increment must be a valid numeric value, including a double-precision floating-point number.

ZPOPMAX.summary: ZPOPMAX removes and returns the highest-scoring members in a sorted set. It removes one member by default or up to the requested count.
ZPOPMAX.explanation: ZPOPMAX removes members from a sorted set and returns them with their scores. It removes the highest-scoring member first; with a count, it returns up to that many members in descending score order.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key that contains the sorted set.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Optional maximum number of members to remove. Defaults to 1.

ZPOPMAX.returns: An array containing the removed members and their scores. With RESP2 and RESP3, the result is an array reply.

example.title: Pop the highest scores
example.code:
ZADD myzset 1 one
ZADD myzset 2 two
ZADD myzset 3 three
ZPOPMAX myzset 2
example.explanation: Adds three members, then removes and returns the two members with the highest scores: three first, then two.

useCases.title: Consume highest-priority jobs
useCases.scenario: A worker needs to claim the highest-priority jobs from a sorted set and remove them atomically.

useCases.title: Process ranked items in batches
useCases.scenario: An application keeps only pending top-ranked items by removing the highest scores in batches.

useCases.title: Pop one ranked item
useCases.scenario: A queue stores work items by score, and a consumer needs one item at a time without leaving it available.

interview.question: What does ZPOPMAX do?
interview.answer: It removes and returns the highest-scoring members from the sorted set at the given key. Without count, it removes one member.
interview.followUp: How are several returned members ordered? They are returned from highest score to lower score.

interview.question: What is the time complexity of ZPOPMAX?
interview.answer: The command uses O(log(N)*M) time. N is the number of members in the sorted set, and M is the number removed.
interview.followUp: What happens when M is one? The work is O(log(N)).

interview.question: What are the arguments?
interview.answer: The syntax is ZPOPMAX key [count]. The key names the sorted set, and count optionally sets the maximum number of members to remove.
interview.followUp: What if count exceeds the sorted set size? Redis returns the available members without an error.

keyPoints: ZPOPMAX both returns and removes members. It is not a read-only lookup.
Leaving out count removes one member.
With multiple results, the highest score appears first.
The required key argument identifies the sorted set to change.
The optional count limits how many members Redis removes.
ZPOPMAX was added in Redis Open Source 5.0.0.
gotchas: A count larger than the number of members does not cause an error. Redis returns all available members.
If the command removes the final member, Redis also deletes the sorted-set key.

ZPOPMIN.summary: ZPOPMIN removes and returns members with the lowest scores from a sorted set. It removes one member by default, or up to the optional count.
ZPOPMIN.explanation: ZPOPMIN changes a sorted set by removing its lowest-scoring members and returning each member with its score. You can give a count to remove several members; results are ordered from the lowest score upward. If the operation removes the last member, Redis deletes the sorted-set key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The name of the key that stores the sorted set.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Optional number of members to remove and return. Defaults to 1.

ZPOPMIN.returns: An array containing the popped members and their scores. In RESP2 and RESP3, it is an array reply.

example.title: Pop the lowest-scoring member
example.code:
ZADD tasks 10 "low"
ZADD tasks 20 "high"
ZPOPMIN tasks
ZRANGE tasks 0 -1 WITHSCORES
example.explanation: Adds two members, removes the member with the lowest score, then shows the remaining sorted set.

useCases.title: Priority queues
useCases.scenario: Remove the next lowest-priority item from a sorted set while retrieving its score.

useCases.title: Batch processing
useCases.scenario: Process several lowest-ranked members in one command.

useCases.title: Ordered work consumption
useCases.scenario: Consume members in ascending score order until the sorted set is empty.

interview.question: What does ZPOPMIN do?
interview.answer: ZPOPMIN removes and returns up to count members with the smallest scores from the sorted set at key. Without count, it removes one member.
interview.followUp: How are multiple results ordered? They are returned from the lowest score to higher scores.

interview.question: What are its arguments?
interview.answer: The command uses the syntax ZPOPMIN key [count]. key is required, while count is an optional integer.
interview.followUp: What happens when count is greater than the set size? Redis does not return an error and removes the members that exist.

interview.question: What is its time complexity?
interview.answer: Its time complexity is O(log(N)*M), where N is the number of sorted-set elements and M is the number popped. It is a write command in the sorted-set group.
interview.followUp: When does the key disappear? Redis deletes it when the last member is popped.

keyPoints: It both removes members and returns them, so it is not a read-only range query.
For multiple popped members, the result starts with the lowest score.
The key identifies the sorted set that Redis changes.
count limits how many members Redis removes and returns.
The running time depends on the set size and the number of members removed.
Redis Open Source added this command in version 5.0.0.
gotchas: A count larger than the number of members does not cause an error; Redis removes all available members.
If you omit count, Redis removes one member.
Popping the final member also removes the sorted-set key.

ZRANGE.summary: Returns members from a sorted set selected by rank, score, or lexicographical range. Optional reverse ordering, pagination, and score output support ranking, filtering, and windowed reads.
ZRANGE.explanation: ZRANGE reads members from a sorted set using an index range by default. BYSCORE changes the bounds to scores, BYLEX changes them to lexicographical member values, REV reverses the result order, LIMIT paginates matches, and WITHSCORES includes each member's score.
ZRANGE.syntax: ZRANGE key start stop [BYSCORE | BYLEX] [REV] [LIMIT offset count] [WITHSCORES]

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Name of the sorted-set key.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Starting rank, score bound, or lexicographical bound, depending on the selected mode.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.description: Ending rank, score bound, or lexicographical bound, depending on the selected mode.

parameters.name: BYSCORE | BYLEX
parameters.description: Select score-based or lexicographical bounds.

parameters.name: REV
parameters.description: Reverse the result order and interpretation of the range.

parameters.name: LIMIT offset count
parameters.description: Skip offset matches and return up to count matches.

parameters.name: WITHSCORES
parameters.description: Include scores alongside members.

ZRANGE.returns: An array of matching sorted-set members; with WITHSCORES, each member is accompanied by its score. A non-overlapping range returns an empty array.

example.title: Rank and score range queries
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 120 alice 95 bob 110 carol
ZRANGE leaderboard 0 -1 WITHSCORES
ZRANGE leaderboard 100 120 BYSCORE REV LIMIT 0 2
example.explanation: Adds three members, lists them by rank with scores, then retrieves up to two members whose scores fall in the selected range in descending score order.

useCases.title: Leaderboards and ranking pages
useCases.scenario: Fetch a page of leaderboard entries by rank, optionally including their scores.

useCases.title: Score-range filtering
useCases.scenario: Select records whose sorted-set scores fall between two bounds.

useCases.title: Lexicographical indexing
useCases.scenario: Use equal-score members and BYLEX bounds to retrieve a name or identifier interval.

interview.question: How does default ZRANGE indexing work?
interview.answer: By default, ZRANGE interprets start and stop as zero-based rank indexes, and both bounds are inclusive. Negative indexes count backward from the end, with -1 representing the final member.
interview.followUp: How can it retrieve the highest-scoring members? Use REV together with BYSCORE, then apply LIMIT, for example: ZRANGE key +inf -inf BYSCORE REV LIMIT 0 10.

interview.question: How does a score-based query differ from the default query?
interview.answer: BYSCORE makes the two bounds score limits instead of indexes. Score bounds can be inclusive or exclusive, and special values such as -inf and +inf can represent unbounded ends.
interview.followUp: How would you return scores as well? Add WITHSCORES; the response alternates each returned member with its score.

interview.question: What options control ordering, pagination, and returned data?
interview.answer: ZRANGE supports BYLEX for member-name ranges, REV for reverse ordering, LIMIT offset count for pagination, and WITHSCORES for returning scores. Its complexity is O(log(N)+M), where M is the number of returned elements.
interview.followUp: Why should a caller avoid unrestricted large reads? Because M grows with the result size, so limiting the requested range reduces work and response size.

keyPoints: The command reads members from the sorted set stored at the specified key.
One command supports rank-based, score-based, and lexicographical range selection.
Negative rank indexes address members relative to the set's end.
An oversized ending rank is clamped to the last available member.
gotchas: The start and stop bounds are inclusive. Use a parenthesis on score or lexicographical bounds when an exclusive boundary is required.
Invalid or non-overlapping index ranges return an empty list rather than an error.

ZRANGEBYSCORE.summary: Returns members from a sorted set whose scores are within a chosen range. Use WITHSCORES for scores and LIMIT for paging; for new code, use ZRANGE with BYSCORE because this command is deprecated since Redis 6.2.0.
ZRANGEBYSCORE.explanation: ZRANGEBYSCORE reads members from a sorted set when their scores fall between min and max. The bounds include their endpoint scores unless you prefix a bound with (, and you can page through matches with LIMIT.
ZRANGEBYSCORE.syntax: ZRANGEBYSCORE key min max [WITHSCORES] [LIMIT offset count]

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The sorted-set key.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: The minimum score. Inclusive unless prefixed with (. Use -inf for no lower bound.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The maximum score. Inclusive unless prefixed with (. Use +inf for no upper bound.

parameters.name: WITHSCORES
parameters.description: Return each member together with its score.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Skip this many matching members.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Return up to this many members. A negative value returns all remaining members.

ZRANGEBYSCORE.returns: An array of members in the score range, optionally followed by their scores.

example.title: Read members by score
example.code:
ZADD scores 1 one 2 two 3 three
ZRANGEBYSCORE scores 1 2 WITHSCORES
# 1) "one"
# 2) "1"
# 3) "two"
# 4) "2"
example.explanation: This adds three members, then returns the members whose scores are from 1 through 2, including their scores.

useCases.title: Score-range queries
useCases.scenario: Read items whose numeric scores fall between two limits.

useCases.title: Pagination
useCases.scenario: Read a fixed page of matching members.

useCases.title: Open-ended ranges
useCases.scenario: Read members from the lowest or highest score up to a chosen bound.

useCases.title: Weighted selection
useCases.scenario: Select weighted results using cumulative scores.

interview.question: What does ZRANGEBYSCORE do?
interview.answer: It returns sorted-set members whose scores are between min and max. Both bounds are inclusive by default, and WITHSCORES adds each member's score to the result.
interview.followUp: How would you exclude the lower bound? Pass it as ( followed by the score, such as (10.

interview.question: How do you express unbounded or exclusive ranges?
interview.answer: Use -inf for an unbounded lower limit and +inf for an unbounded upper limit. This lets you query all members or one side of a score range without knowing the set's extreme score.
interview.followUp: How would you return only scores greater than 10? Use (10 as min and +inf as max.

interview.question: How does LIMIT affect the result?
interview.answer: LIMIT offset count skips offset matching members and returns at most count. A negative count returns all remaining matches after the offset.
interview.followUp: What is the newer replacement for this command? Use ZRANGE with the BYSCORE option, which supports score-range queries.

keyPoints: The command selects members by their sorted-set scores.
The command needs a key, a minimum score, and a maximum score.
WITHSCORES includes each returned member's score.
LIMIT supports offset-based paging through matching members.
Use -inf or +inf when one side of the score range has no limit.
Prefix a bound with ( to exclude that endpoint.
The work depends on the sorted-set size and the number of returned members.
gotchas: ZRANGEBYSCORE is deprecated since Redis 6.2.0. Use ZRANGE with BYSCORE for new code.
With LIMIT, a negative count does not limit the number of returned members after the offset.
Bounds include matching endpoint scores unless you add ( before the bound.

ZRANK.summary: Returns a member's zero-based rank in a sorted set, ordered by ascending score. WITHSCORE also returns that member's score.
ZRANK.explanation: ZRANK looks up a member in the sorted set stored at the key. It orders members by score from low to high and uses zero-based positions, so the lowest score has rank 0. WITHSCORE also returns the member's score. Use ZREVRANK for high-to-low order.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key that stores the sorted set.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: The sorted-set member whose rank to return.

parameters.name: WITHSCORE
parameters.description: Optional keyword that also returns the member's score.

ZRANK.returns: Without WITHSCORE, an integer reply gives the member's rank. With WITHSCORE, an array reply contains the rank and score. A missing key or member returns nil in RESP2 or null in RESP3.

example.title: Find a sorted-set rank
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 10 alice 20 bob 15 cara
ZRANK leaderboard alice
ZRANK leaderboard bob WITHSCORE
example.explanation: Adds three members, then returns Alice's zero-based rank and Bob's rank together with his score.

useCases.title: Read a leaderboard position
useCases.scenario: Show a user's position on a leaderboard ordered from the lowest score to the highest.

useCases.title: Read rank and score
useCases.scenario: Get both a member's position and current score in one command.

useCases.title: Test membership
useCases.scenario: Check whether a member exists in a sorted set by testing for a nil or null reply.

interview.question: What does ZRANK return?
interview.answer: ZRANK returns a member's zero-based position in a sorted set when scores are ordered from low to high. It returns a nil or null reply when the key or member is missing.
interview.followUp: How would you rank from high to low? Use ZREVRANK instead of ZRANK.

interview.question: What is the syntax of ZRANK?
interview.answer: The command is `ZRANK key member [WITHSCORE]`. The key identifies the sorted set, and member identifies the item whose rank is requested.
interview.followUp: What extra data does WITHSCORE provide? It adds the member's score to the reply.

interview.question: How does WITHSCORE change the reply?
interview.answer: Without WITHSCORE, the command returns an integer rank. With WITHSCORE, it returns the rank and score in an array reply.
interview.followUp: What is its time complexity? The operation takes O(log(N)) time.

keyPoints: ZRANK finds a member's position using ascending score order.
The lowest-scoring member has rank 0.
WITHSCORE adds the member's score to the result.
Use ZREVRANK when scores must be ordered from highest to lowest.
The command's time complexity is O(log(N)).
WITHSCORE is available starting with Redis 7.2.0.
gotchas: A missing key or member returns a nil or null reply, not a numeric rank.
Ranks start at 0, so the first member is not rank 1.

ZREM.summary: ZREM removes one or more members from a Redis sorted set. It returns the number of members that were actually removed.
ZREM.explanation: ZREM removes one or more named members from the sorted set stored at a key. Redis ignores names that are not present and returns how many existing members it removed.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The name of the key that stores the sorted set.

parameters.name: member [member ...]
parameters.description: One or more member names to remove.

ZREM.returns: An integer: the number of existing sorted-set members removed. Missing members are not counted.

example.title: Remove one member
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 10 alice 20 bob
ZREM leaderboard bob
ZRANGE leaderboard 0 -1 WITHSCORES
example.explanation: This adds two members, removes bob, then lists the remaining sorted-set members with scores.

useCases.title: Update a leaderboard
useCases.scenario: Remove a user from a leaderboard after the user leaves a competition.

useCases.title: Clean up entries
useCases.scenario: Delete expired or invalid entries when their member names are known.

useCases.title: Batch removal
useCases.scenario: Remove several selected members with one Redis command.

interview.question: What does ZREM do, and what is its time complexity?
interview.answer: ZREM removes the requested members from a sorted set. Its time complexity is O(M*log(N)), where M is the number of requested members and N is the sorted-set size.
interview.followUp: What happens when a requested member is absent? Redis ignores it, and the returned count does not include it.

interview.question: What does ZREM return?
interview.answer: The command returns an integer equal to the number of requested members that were actually present and removed. Missing members do not increase this number.
interview.followUp: Can the return value be used to detect whether every requested member existed? Yes, compare it with the number of requested members, while accounting for duplicate inputs if relevant to the client.

interview.question: What arguments does ZREM accept?
interview.answer: Its syntax is ZREM key member [member ...]. The key identifies the sorted set, and the command accepts one or more member names.
interview.followUp: How does ZREM behave if the key has another type? It returns an error instead of removing a value.

keyPoints: Use ZREM to remove named members from a sorted set.
A member that is not present causes no error and is not counted.
Redis supports removing several members in one command.
The result counts only members that Redis actually removed.
The command was introduced in Redis Open Source 1.2.0.
gotchas: The command fails if the key exists but contains a different Redis data type.
If the removal leaves no members, Redis deletes the sorted-set key.

ZREVRANGE.summary: Returns members from a Redis sorted set by rank, from highest score to lowest. The range uses zero-based, inclusive indexes and can include scores.
ZREVRANGE.explanation: ZREVRANGE reads members from a Redis sorted set by zero-based rank, starting with the highest score. The stop rank is included, and equal scores are ordered in descending lexicographical order. Use WITHSCORES to include each member's score.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key that stores the sorted set.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The zero-based starting rank. Negative values count from the end.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.description: The inclusive zero-based ending rank. Negative values count from the end.

parameters.name: WITHSCORES
parameters.description: Optional token that includes scores in the reply.

ZREVRANGE.returns: An array of members in the requested range, optionally including their scores when WITHSCORES is used.

example.title: Get the top two members
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 10 alice 25 bob 18 carol
ZREVRANGE leaderboard 0 1 WITHSCORES
example.explanation: Adds three members, then returns the two highest-scoring members with their scores.

useCases.title: Top scores
useCases.scenario: Read the highest-ranked members for a leaderboard.

useCases.title: Reverse pagination
useCases.scenario: Fetch a page of members by descending rank.

useCases.title: Ranked results with scores
useCases.scenario: Get member-score pairs for reporting or display.

interview.question: What does ZREVRANGE return?
interview.answer: It returns members from a sorted set between the start and stop ranks, ordered from highest to lowest score. Both indexes are zero-based, and the stop index is included.
interview.followUp: How would you return the same order with the newer command? Use ZRANGE with the REV option.

interview.question: How do the indexes work?
interview.answer: The start and stop arguments are rank indexes. A negative index counts from the end of the sorted set; -1 is the member with the highest score in this reverse ordering.
interview.followUp: What does stop = -1 mean? It selects through the last member in the reverse-ordered result.

interview.question: What does WITHSCORES do, and what is the complexity?
interview.answer: WITHSCORES adds the score after each returned member. The command has time complexity O(log(N)+M), where N is the set size and M is the number of returned elements.
interview.followUp: What is the cost of returning a fixed small number of results? The logarithmic term remains, while M is bounded by that small result size.

keyPoints: Use it to read a rank range from a sorted set in descending score order.
The first result has the highest score.
Members with the same score are sorted from larger to smaller lexicographical order.
start is zero-based, and negative values count backward from the end.
WITHSCORES returns each member together with its score.
Its time complexity depends on the sorted-set size and the number of results returned.
gotchas: ZREVRANGE is deprecated since Redis 6.2.0. For new code, use ZRANGE with REV instead.
The stop rank is inclusive. Negative ranks count from the end, so -1 refers to the last member in the selected order.

ZREVRANK.summary: ZRANK returns a member's zero-based rank in a sorted set, ordered by ascending score. WITHSCORE also returns that member's score.
ZREVRANK.explanation: ZRANK searches the sorted set at a key for a member. It orders members from the lowest score to the highest, so the lowest-scoring member has index 0. WITHSCORE also returns the member's score. If the key or member is missing, the command returns a null result.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key that stores the sorted set.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: The member whose rank Redis should return.

parameters.name: WITHSCORE
parameters.description: Also return the member's score.

ZREVRANK.returns: Without WITHSCORE, Redis returns the zero-based rank as an integer. With WITHSCORE, it returns the rank and score. If the key or member does not exist, it returns nil in RESP2 or null in RESP3.

example.title: Find a member's rank
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 10 alice 25 bob 15 carol
ZRANK leaderboard carol
ZRANK leaderboard bob WITHSCORE
example.explanation: Adds three members, finds Carol's zero-based ascending rank, then finds Bob's rank and score.

useCases.title: Ascending rankings
useCases.scenario: You need the position of an item when the smallest score should come first.

useCases.title: Rank with score
useCases.scenario: You need both the position and the stored score in one command.

useCases.title: Membership lookup
useCases.scenario: You need to check whether a sorted-set member exists while reading its position.

interview.question: What does ZRANK return?
interview.answer: ZRANK returns a member's zero-based position in a sorted set when scores are ordered from low to high. Without WITHSCORE, the result is an integer, or null when the key or member is missing.
interview.followUp: How do you obtain descending rank? Use ZREVRANK, which orders scores from high to low.

interview.question: What is the syntax of ZRANK?
interview.answer: The syntax is `ZRANK key member [WITHSCORE]`. `key` names the sorted set, `member` names the item, and WITHSCORE is optional.
interview.followUp: What does WITHSCORE add? It adds the member's score to the rank in the reply.

interview.question: What is the command's complexity and how does WITHSCORE change the reply?
interview.answer: ZRANK has time complexity O(log(N)). With WITHSCORE, the reply contains both the rank and the score; without it, the reply contains only the rank.
interview.followUp: What happens if the requested member is absent? Redis returns a null reply in RESP3, or a nil reply in RESP2.

keyPoints: ZRANK returns a member's position in ascending score order.
WITHSCORE adds the matching member's score to the result.
The key argument identifies the sorted set to search.
The member argument identifies which sorted-set item to rank.
The documented time complexity is O(log(N)).
WITHSCORE is available starting with Redis 7.2.0.
gotchas: Ranks start at 0, not 1. The member with the lowest score is rank 0.
A missing key or member produces a null result.
ZRANK orders from low to high. Use ZREVRANK when you need high-to-low order.

ZSCORE.summary: Returns the score of one member in a Redis sorted set. It returns nil when the member or key does not exist.
ZSCORE.explanation: ZSCORE looks up one member in the sorted set stored at a key. It returns that member's score. If either the member or the key is missing, the result is nil. The lookup takes constant time.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The name of the key that holds the sorted set.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: The member whose score to return.

ZSCORE.returns: The member's score as a double-precision floating-point value. RESP2 represents it as a bulk string, while RESP3 uses a double. If the member or key does not exist, the result is nil.

example.title: Read a member score
example.code:
ZADD leaderboard 42 alice
ZSCORE leaderboard alice
example.explanation: This adds `alice` with score 42, then returns her score.

useCases.title: Read a leaderboard score
useCases.scenario: You need the current numeric value for one ranked item.

useCases.title: Check membership and score
useCases.scenario: You need to check whether a sorted-set member has an assigned score.

useCases.title: Read a task priority
useCases.scenario: You store numeric priorities in a sorted set and need one item's priority.

interview.question: What does ZSCORE do?
interview.answer: ZSCORE returns the score for one member in a sorted set. Its time complexity is O(1).
interview.followUp: What happens when the member is absent? The command returns nil, including when the key itself is absent.

interview.question: What arguments does ZSCORE take?
interview.answer: The command is `ZSCORE key member`. `key` identifies the sorted set, and `member` identifies the member whose score should be read.
interview.followUp: How would you read several scores? Use the related ZMSCORE command when you need scores for multiple members.

interview.question: What type does ZSCORE return?
interview.answer: In RESP2, the score is returned as a bulk string containing a double-precision floating-point number. In RESP3, it is returned as a double; a missing member still returns nil.
interview.followUp: Why can client APIs show different types? Clients map the Redis protocol reply into language-specific types, such as a nullable number or an optional floating-point value.

keyPoints: Use ZSCORE to read one member's score from a sorted set.
The key argument must identify the sorted set to inspect.
The member argument selects which sorted-set entry to read.
Redis has supported this command since version 1.2.0.
The lookup has constant time complexity, O(1).
The command is classified as read-only, sorted-set related, and fast by ACL category.
gotchas: A missing member and a missing key both produce nil, so handle the missing-result case.
